classification.difficultyReason: Use the shared 32 mm edge and equal heights, double the trapezium top to obtain its base, then add two standard component areas.

inlines.text: A logo consists of a parallelogram on top of a trapezium, as shown.
The parallelogram has height 16 mm and base 32 mm.
The trapezium is the same height as the parallelogram and its base is twice the length of its top.
Find the area of the logo, in square millimetres.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6, logo below the stem at the left
spec.description: Unshaded connected parallelogram and trapezium logo, shared base labelled 32 mm, both perpendicular heights labelled 16 mm with right-angle markers, lower base labelled 2×32 mm.
spec.mathematics: Shared base 32 mm; both perpendicular heights 16 mm; lower base is twice the shared base.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no supplied answer, calculated dimensions or solution annotations.

answer.worked:
The trapezium's top is the shared $32\text{ mm}$ edge, and its height is $16\text{ mm}$. Let $A_1$ be the parallelogram's area and $A_2$ the trapezium's area.

$$\begin{align*}b&=2\times32\\b&=64\text{ mm}\\A_1&=32\times16\\A_1&=512\text{ mm}^2\\A_2&=\frac{16(32+64)}{2}\\A_2&=768\text{ mm}^2\\A_{\text{Total}}&=512+768\\A_{\text{Total}}&=1280\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$
